newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG UPSET BY AMATEURS AFTER LEADING 4-1.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG UPSET BY AMATEURS AFTER LEADING 4-1.

text.p: Paris St Germain crashed out of the French Cup 4-3 on penalties to Clermont after the fourth division side had recovered from 4-1 to draw 4-4 in normal time of their third round tie on Saturday.

Goalkeeper Olivier Enjoiras, a clothes salesman, put the amateurs into the quarter-finals by saving the penalties of defender Paul Le Guen and midfielder Vincent Guerin as gloom descended over PSG five days before they resume their defence of the European Cup Winners' Cup.

It was the second major upset in 24 hours, following Auxerre's stunning loss to second division Troyes five days before they meet Borussia Dortmund away in the first leg of their European Cup quarter-final.
Holders and league champions Auxerre were Troyes' second top flight victims. In the previous round, they won 1-0 at Rennes, who have one of the best home records in the first division.

PSG, who also met sides from the lower divisions in the previous rounds, looked on their way to a comfortable victory after first half goals by midfielder Benoit Cauet and striker Julio Cesar Dely Valdes.
Clermont pulled one back with a penalty by Bessaque in the 53rd minute, but Brazil's Rai and France striker Patrice Loko extended PSG's lead to 4-1 by the 68th minute.
A minute later, however, striker Chastang showed PSG his team were not beaten yet when he pulled another goal back.

In the final seven minutes Clermont pulled level through captain Le Bellec, the only professional in the home side, and a last-minute own goal by France midfielder Bruno N'Gotty. There were no goals in extra time.
PSG are at home to AEK Athens in the first leg of their Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final on Thursday.
There will be no repeat of the League Cup final in the French Cup final following Strasbourg's shock 1-0 elimination by third division Creteil.
Strasbourg, who meet Bordeaux in the League Cup final on April 12, fell behind to a goal by man-of-the-match Kharchaoui in the last minute of the first half.

Despite dominating the second half, the first division side were unable to equalise and Creteil nearly scored a second through striker Franco Vignola, who was foiled by a superb save by Strasbourg's Slovakian goalkeeper Alexander Vencel.
Bordeaux moved a step closer to a domestic cup double when they reached the quarter-finals by beating Cannes 1-0 at home.

Striker Didier Tholot scored the winner for Bordeaux. Kaba Diawara's header from midfielder Francois Grenet's cross from the right was saved by Francois Lemasson, but the Cannes keeper was on his knees when Tholot blasted home the rebound.

Bordeaux's veteran Belgian goalkeeper Gilbert Bodart, the hero of their League Cup semifinal penalty shoot-out win over Montpellier, saved a point blank header from Cannes striker Cedric Mouret early in the second half.
Tholot's substitute Jean-Pierre Papin put the ball in the net with a trademark volley three minutes after coming on but the referee blew up for offside by the former France striker.
Lille are at home to Montpellier on Sunday.
